memory_candidates: When a plan's prior phase (here: v2 Phase 10) records a verdict ruling out a proof-obligation sub-case ('R1: case (a) does not bite') based on prose reasoning without a completed Lean proof of the downstream consumer, treat that verdict as provisional, not settled -- confirm it by actually attempting the consumer's proof (or at minimum inspecting the live goal state at the point the verdict is invoked) before building further phases on top of it. Here the verdict's own reasoning ('the consumer only ever queries the witness case through the same unwrapped-membership fact') was a plausible-sounding but ultimately incorrect inference; the actual Lean goal state (via lean_goal) immediately showed no hypothesis closes it.

Cslib/Logics/Modal/Tableau/LoopChecking.lean and Cslib/Logics/Modal/Tableau/FrameSoundness.lean have no import relationship in either direction (both only import Cslib.Logics.Modal.Tableau.FrameRules and similar siblings) despite FrameSoundness.lean's docstrings referencing LoopChecking.lean concepts in prose. A lemma needing declarations from both must add an explicit public import in whichever file has the narrower existing import set; verify acyclicity with a full lake build rather than assuming the prose cross-references imply an existing import edge.

A driver-invariant stated purely in terms of a `keys : List (WorldIndex x Finset _)` bookkeeping structure (not `b`/`acc`) -- e.g. 'world 0's recorded key is always empty' -- is provable as a tiny standalone auxiliary (def + trivial entry lemma) even when its full step-preservation proof is deferred; useful to land the entry half early and let a later phase (doing the big combined induction anyway) supply preservation without re-deriving the whole invariant from scratch.
